name: @guardbee/mcp-slopsquat-scanner
description: MCP server that checks every dependency declared in package.json/requirements.txt/pyproject.toml against the real npm/PyPI registry -- flags names that don't exist at all (likely LLM-hallucinated dependencies an attacker may have pre-registered, i.e. slopsquatting) and names that exist but were only very recently published
long_description: LLM coding assistants hallucinate plausible-sounding package names at a measurable rate (research puts open-source models around 21.7%), and attackers pre-register those exact names on npm/PyPI so the next developer who copies the same suggestion installs their code instead of getting an install error -- this is 'slopsquatting'. This package parses a project's own manifest files (package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml -- direct dependencies only, not the full resolved lockfile tree) and checks each declared name against the real registry over the network: a name that doesn't exist at all is flagged critical, and a name that exists but was only published in the last 30 days is flagged low (informational -- could be a legitimate new package or a name registered just ahead of an expected hallucination). No API key required; queries the public, unauthenticated npm and PyPI registry APIs directly.
